Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The rain has ceased, so the children can finally go out to play.
The construction noise is ceasing at six o'clock every evening.
Ceasing to smoke is one of the hardest but most rewarding decisions a person can make.
The bus service ceases after midnight, so plan your return trip early.

definition: The flat upper surface that forms the top inside of a room, opposite the floor.
extra_senses: (meteorology) altitude of the lowest layer of clouds
an upper limit on what is allowed
examples: The ceiling fan in our classroom makes a squeaky noise whenever it starts to spin.
Our old house has high ceilings, so the rooms stay cool even in the summer.
A small crack appeared in the ceiling after the heavy rain last night.
The painter covered the ceiling with white paint before starting on the walls.
The shop's ceiling lights were switched on early because the afternoon sky was dark.

definition: To do something enjoyable to mark a special event, such as a birthday, success or festival.
extra_senses: have a celebration
assign great social importance to
examples: We celebrated my grandmother's seventieth birthday with a big lunch and some music.
The team celebrated their victory by dancing on the field after the final match.
Families across the country celebrate Pohela Boishakh with new clothes and special food.
My friends and I celebrated the end of our exams with a movie and a cup of tea.
The company celebrated its anniversary with a small party for all its staff members.

form_sentences.sentence: Our class has celebrated the end of exams with a small picnic.
The whole village is celebrating the harvest with music and dancing.
Celebrating a friend's good news with a meal makes everyone happy.
My father celebrates his birthday with a simple family dinner each year.
We plan to celebrate the new year at the riverside with friends.

definition: A happy event or party held to mark a special occasion or an achievement.
extra_senses: any joyous diversion
the public performance of a sacrament or solemn ceremony with all appropriate ritual
examples: The village held a big celebration when the new school building was finally opened.
Our wedding celebration lasted three days, and the whole neighbourhood joined in.
We had a small celebration at home after my sister passed her final exam.
The fireworks at the celebration lit up the sky over the river at midnight.
The company's annual celebration will be held in the hotel ballroom this December.

form_sentences.sentence: Families hold small celebrations when a child passes an important exam.
We will celebrate my cousin's wedding with a small family gathering.

definition: Quickness of movement or action; speed.
examples: The firefighters arrived with celerity and put out the fire before it spread.
She answered every email with celerity, which impressed her manager.
The waiter moved with surprising celerity between the crowded tables.
The authorities responded to the flood with celerity, sending boats within hours.
He packed his bag with such celerity that he almost forgot his passport.

definition: The state of choosing not to marry or have sexual relations, usually for religious reasons.
extra_senses: abstaining from sexual relations (as because of religious vows)
examples: Monks in many traditions take a vow of celibacy when they join a monastery.
The documentary explained why some religious orders require celibacy from their members.
He chose celibacy and devoted his whole life to teaching poor children.
The priest spoke openly about the challenges of celibacy in a modern world.
In the novel, the old teacher lives in celibacy, surrounded only by books.

definition: The smallest unit of living matter, which makes up every plant and animal and carries out life functions.
extra_senses: (biology) the basic structural and functional unit of all organisms; they may exist as independent units of life (as in monads) or may form colonies or tissues as in higher plants and animals
a device that delivers an electric current as the result of a chemical reaction
examples: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to every part of the body.
Plant cells have a rigid wall that gives the leaves their shape and strength.
Under the microscope, we could clearly see the nucleus inside each cell.
Skin cells replace themselves regularly, so a small cut usually heals within a few days.
The biology exam asked us to label the parts of an animal cell in the diagram.

form_sentences.sentence: Cellular damage can build up in the body from years of smoking.

definition: A portable telephone that connects to a wireless network, so you can call and message people anywhere.
examples: I forgot my cell phone at home, so I could not check the bus timetable.
My cell phone battery runs out quickly if I watch videos during the long bus ride.
Please switch off your cell phone before you enter the examination hall.
The shopkeeper sells cell phone chargers and cheap earphones near the market gate.
Grandmother learned to send messages on her cell phone to stay in touch with us.

definition: Strong public disapproval, or an official statement that criticizes someone for their behavior.
extra_senses: rebuke formally
the state of being excommunicated
examples: The committee issued a formal censure against the club treasurer for misusing funds.
He faced public censure after posting insulting comments about the team.
The doctor's careless mistake brought censure from the medical board.
The company's advertisement drew widespread censure from parents and teachers.
Her work was beyond censure; every report was accurate and on time.

form_sentences.sentence: The council issued two censures after the official ignored the complaints.

definition: A small coin or unit of money worth one hundredth of a dollar or of a similar currency.
extra_senses: a coin worth one-hundredth of the value of the basic unit
examples: The shopkeeper gave me back the change, but he was missing two cents.
The imported pen cost only a few cents more than the local one.
We do not have a single cent left after paying for the hotel and the taxi.
Cents are the small units that make up a dollar in many countries.
My cousin working abroad sends money home, and the exchange rate changes by a few cents each day.

definition: A metric unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre, often used to measure small objects.
examples: The tailor measured my waist and wrote the length down in centimetres.
The seedling was only three centimetres tall after a week in the nursery.
Please measure the shelf in centimetres before you buy the wooden board.
A two-centimetre cut on my finger needed three stitches at the clinic.
The fish in the tank grew from five centimetres to fifteen in only six months.

definition: Most important and necessary, or located in the middle of something.
extra_senses: in or near a center or constituting a center; the inner area
a workplace that serves as a telecommunications facility where lines from telephones can be connected together to permit communication
examples: Reading every day is central to improving your vocabulary for the admission test.
Our hotel is in a central location, close to the bus station and the bazaar.
The manager played a central role in negotiating the deal with the new supplier.
The central market is crowded every morning with vendors and shoppers.
Trust is central to a healthy friendship, and honesty builds it over time.

form_sentences.sentence: Our new flat is more central, so it is easier to reach the office.
The centrality of a strong vocabulary to reading success is widely recognised.
The new hospital is centrally located near the main bus station.

definition: The middle point or inner part of something, or a place where a particular activity happens.
extra_senses: move into the center
an area that is approximately central within some larger region
examples: Our house is near the city centre, so buses and shops are always within walking distance.
A shopping centre opened near the railway station and attracts large crowds every weekend.
The teacher stood at the centre of the classroom and explained the new formula.
The earthquake's centre was far away, but we still felt the ground shake for a few seconds.
Our village has a community centre where children learn to paint and read books.

form_sentences.sentence: The community center near our house offers free English classes on Fridays.
The central library is open until nine o'clock on weekdays.
Most ads center on the product's price rather than its quality.

definition: A period of one hundred years, counted from a fixed starting point in history.
extra_senses: ten 10s
examples: The old school building was constructed more than a century ago by local landowners.
Many scientific discoveries were made in the last century, and they changed daily life completely.
The mango tree in our yard has stood for almost a century, and it still gives fruit.
The city's oldest library has kept its books safe for more than a century.
Our town has changed a lot over the past century, with new roads and tall buildings.

form_sentences.sentence: Tourists admire old buildings that have stood for many centuries.

definition: Involving or appealing to careful thinking rather than emotion; also, relating to the brain.
extra_senses: of or relating to the cerebrum or brain
examples: Chess is a cerebral game that rewards patience and careful planning.
He is a cerebral writer whose novels make readers think more than they feel.
The film was too cerebral for me; I wanted action, not long conversations about ideas.
Our cerebral math teacher loves puzzles and can solve most of them in his head.
She prefers a cerebral approach to problems and makes lists before every decision.

form_sentences.sentence: The novel is more cerebral than the film, focusing on ideas instead of action.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain and controls thinking and language.
The film engages viewers cerebrally, asking them to think long after the credits.

definition: A formal event or set of actions performed on an important or special occasion.
extra_senses: any activity that is performed in an especially solemn elaborate or formal way
the proper or conventional behavior on some solemn occasion
examples: The graduation ceremony was held in the university hall, and parents filled the seats.
The opening ceremony for the new bridge started with a short speech and a ribbon cutting.
The school held a simple award ceremony at the end of the year for its best students.
Our family attended the wedding ceremony in the village, and the food was delicious.
The ceremony began with a few traditional songs, and then the guests were served tea.

form_sentences.sentence: The university holds two graduation ceremonies every year for its students.
The ceremonial opening of the new library was attended by the vice-chancellor.

definition: Having no doubt about something; completely convinced that something is true or will happen.
extra_senses: having or feeling no doubt or uncertainty; confident and assured
established beyond doubt or question; definitely known
examples: I am certain that I left my keys on the table, but I cannot find them now.
Are you certain about the date of the exam, or should we check the notice board?
She felt certain that she would pass the interview, because she had prepared well.
Make certain that the gate is locked before you go to bed tonight.
The doctor was certain the medicine would work, so the family felt relieved.

form_sentences.sentence: The certain tone in his voice made the whole team trust his plan.
The forecast is more certain today, so we can plan the trip.
Our team will certainly win the quiz if we revise together.
There is no certainty about the result until the official notice is published.

definition: Without any doubt; used to say yes strongly or to emphasise that something will happen.
examples: Certainly, I can help you carry the boxes to the new flat this afternoon.
Our team will certainly win the match if everyone keeps focused on the ball.
The shopkeeper said he would certainly deliver the sofa by Friday evening.
Certainly not, the children must finish their homework before they watch television.
You will certainly need an umbrella today, because the sky is covered with dark clouds.

form_sentences.sentence: It is certain that the bus fare will rise after the holiday.

definition: An official document that confirms a fact, such as a qualification, a birth or a completed course.
extra_senses: present someone with a certificate
a formal declaration that documents a fact of relevance to finance and investment; the holder has a right to receive interest or dividends
examples: Bring your birth certificate and two passport photos when you apply for the new passport.
After completing the computer course, I received a certificate from the institute.
The doctor issued a medical certificate, so my employer allowed me to take leave.
The school gave every student a certificate of attendance at the end of the term.
The company gave its staff a certificate for completing the safety training programme.

form_sentences.sentence: Please bring copies of all your certificates to the job interview.
The officer will certify your copies after checking the original papers.

definition: The dry outer husks of grain that are separated and thrown away, or anything worthless.
extra_senses: material consisting of seed coverings and small pieces of stem or leaves that have been separated from the seeds
foil in thin strips; ejected into the air as a radar countermeasure
examples: Farmers throw the grain into the air so that the wind can blow the chaff away.
To find good information online, you must learn to separate the wheat from the chaff.
My uncle feeds his cattle a mixture of straw and chaff during the dry season.
The editor removed the chaff from the report, leaving only the key facts.
Hundreds of applications arrived, but most were chaff, and only a few candidates stood out.
collocations: separate the wheat from the chaff

definition: A feeling of annoyance or embarrassment caused by failure or disappointment.
extra_senses: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of
examples: To her chagrin, she realized she had left her wallet at home after ordering a big meal.
Much to Rafi's chagrin, his younger cousin beat him at chess again.
He read the email with chagrin, seeing that he had missed a simple spelling mistake.
The team's captain admitted his chagrin at losing to a school with no coach.
To the shopkeeper's chagrin, the customer returned the shirt after wearing it twice.

definition: A series of metal links joined together, or a series of connected things or events.
extra_senses: (chemistry) a series of linked atoms (generally in an organic molecule)
a series of (usually metal) rings or links fitted into one another to make a flexible ligament
examples: She wore a thin gold chain around her neck during the wedding ceremony.
The bicycle chain came loose on the way to school, so I had to fix it quickly.
A chain of small shops now sells fresh vegetables across the district.
A chain of events led to the power cut, starting with a fallen tree near the road.
The dog was tied to a short metal chain beside the gate, so it could not run away.

definition: A seat for one person, usually with a back and sometimes with arms.
extra_senses: the position of professor
act or preside as chair, as of an academic department in a university
examples: Pull up a chair and sit near the window, so you can see the garden.
My grandfather sits in his rocking chair every afternoon, reading the newspaper.
The office chair was too low, so I asked the admin team for a better one.
Please fold the plastic chairs and stack them in the corner after the function.
The students moved their chairs closer to the front to hear the teacher clearly.

form_sentences.sentence: The chairman of the board announced the new budget at the annual meeting.

definition: The person who leads a meeting or the board of an organisation or company.
extra_senses: act or preside as chair, as of an academic department in a university
examples: The chairman opened the meeting by thanking everyone for arriving on time.
The chairman of our housing society collects the monthly service charges from every flat.
Our school chairman invited parents to a meeting about the new admission rules.
The company chairman announced a new training programme for all the factory workers.
A good chairman listens carefully to every opinion before making a final decision.

form_sentences.sentence: She will chair the meeting on Monday because the director is away.
His chairmanship of the company lasted for ten years.

definition: A woman who leads a meeting or the board of an organisation or company.
examples: The chairwoman of the cooperative society announced the new interest rate for loans.
Our college elected a new chairwoman for the student council this afternoon.
The chairwoman thanked the volunteers for their hard work during the flood relief.
My aunt became the chairwoman of the local women's association after many years of service.
The chairwoman asked everyone to speak briefly, so that the meeting finished on time.

form_sentences.sentence: Someone must chair the meeting, so the club asked a volunteer.

definition: Something difficult that tests your ability, skill or strength.
extra_senses: issue a challenge to
a demanding or stimulating situation
examples: Learning to drive in Dhaka traffic is a real challenge for new drivers.
Climbing the hill in the rain was a challenge, but we reached the top.
The biggest challenge for small farmers is the rising cost of fertilizer.
She enjoys a challenge, so she chose the hardest math problem.
Moving to a new country comes with the challenge of learning a new language.

form_sentences.sentence: The challenger took an early lead, surprising the reigning champion in the first round.

definition: A room or enclosed space, often a formal hall used for meetings, or a closed hollow inside something.
extra_senses: place in a chamber
an enclosed volume in the body
examples: The Chamber of Commerce held its annual meeting in a large hall near the port.
The council chamber was full of people waiting for the public hearing to begin.
Sound echoes inside the stone chamber beneath the old fort, so every whisper can be heard.
The heart has four chambers that pump blood around the body without a break.
Some social media users live in an echo chamber, reading only opinions that match their own.

definition: A person who often changes their opinions or behavior to suit the people around them.
extra_senses: a faint constellation in the polar region of the southern hemisphere near Apus and Mensa
lizard of Africa and Madagascar able to change skin color and having a projectile tongue
examples: He is a social chameleon who acts serious with teachers and silly with friends.
A good actor must be a chameleon, changing voice and manner for every role.
At work she was a chameleon, agreeing with whoever had spoken last.
The new manager proved a chameleon, praising the old policy in the morning and the new one at lunch.
My cousin is a chameleon at weddings, easily fitting in with any group of strangers.

form_sentences.sentence: Some actors are chameleons, able to play very different characters with ease.

definition: To support or defend a person, idea or cause publicly and strongly.
extra_senses: protect or fight for as a champion
someone who fights for a cause
examples: Our school librarian has always championed free reading for every student.
She championed the idea of a recycling program until the council approved it.
The charity champions the right of every child to attend school.
He championed his younger brother's dream of becoming an artist, even when their father objected.
Local shopkeepers championed the plan to close the street to cars on weekends.

form_sentences.sentence: The student club is championing recycling across our campus this autumn.
Championing clean rivers takes years of patient work by local volunteers.
She wants to champion women's sports in her school's annual sports day.

definition: An opportunity to do something, or a possibility that something will happen.
extra_senses: an unknown and unpredictable phenomenon that causes an event to result one way rather than another
occurring or appearing or singled out by chance
examples: Give me a chance to explain what happened before you decide who is to blame.
There is a good chance of rain this afternoon, so carry an umbrella with you.
I met my old school friend by chance at the bus stand yesterday morning.
The interview is a great chance to show the employer your skills and experience.
Take a chance on the new restaurant near our house, because the reviews are very good.

form_sentences.sentence: Students who revise every day get more chances to succeed in exams.
Buying a used phone online can be chancy, so check the seller carefully.

definition: To make something different, or to become different in form, nature or state.
extra_senses: undergo a change; become different in essence; losing one's or its original nature
an event that occurs when something passes from one state or phase to another
examples: My cousin changed the layout of her room to make it feel more spacious.
If the bus route changes during Eid, please check the notice at the station.
The teacher said we could change our essay topic before Friday.
Prices at the local market often change quickly after a heavy monsoon rain.
After the new phone update, the screen colours changed completely overnight.
example_usage: Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The bus timetable has changed, so we must check the new times.
The weather is changing quickly, so bring an umbrella to the office.
Changing your password every few months improves online security.
The money changer near the airport offered a fair rate for dollars.

definition: To direct something, such as energy, money or water, toward a particular purpose or place.
extra_senses: transmit or serve as the medium for transmission
a passage for water (or other fluids) to flow through
examples: She channeled her nervous energy into cleaning the whole house before the guests arrived.
Farmers channel river water into the fields through small canals.
The charity channels donations directly to flood victims instead of spending on advertising.
After the breakup, he channeled his sadness into writing songs.
The city plans to channel money into repairing old drains before the monsoon.

form_sentences.sentence: The extra money has been channeled into building a new library for the school.
The river authority is channeling rainwater into the reservoir through new pipes.
Channeling leftover food to shelters reduces waste and helps hungry families.

definition: One of the main sections into which a book is divided, usually with a number or title.
extra_senses: any distinct period in history or in a person's life
a local branch of some fraternity or association
examples: Our teacher asked us to finish chapter five before the next class.
The final chapter of the novel ends with a surprising twist.
I read one chapter every night before bed to relax.
This chapter on photosynthesis includes diagrams that make the process easy to follow.
The book has twelve chapters, and each one tells a story from a different village.

definition: A person or animal in a story, play or film, or a person's qualities of mind.
extra_senses: a characteristic property that defines the apparent individual nature of something
the inherent complex of attributes that determines a persons moral and ethical actions and reactions
examples: The main character in the novel is a clever girl who runs a small tea stall.
Every actor in the drama had a clear character to play on stage.
Our teacher says that honesty is the most important part of a person's character.
The students praised the new principal for her calm and generous character.
In the film, the villain's character changes gradually as the story unfolds.

form_sentences.sentence: The novel has many characters, and each one has a clear personality.
The characteristic smell of jasmine rice fills the kitchen during cooking.
Critics often characterize the film as slow but emotionally powerful.

definition: Typical of a particular person, place or thing, and easily recognised because of it.
extra_senses: a prominent attribute or aspect of something
a distinguishing quality
examples: Her quiet laugh is characteristic of her, and everyone in the family knows it.
The long rain and green fields are characteristic of the Sylhet region in June.
His habit of humming while he cooks is characteristic of my uncle.
The rickshaw's bright paint is characteristic of Dhaka's busy streets.
Tapping a pen during a lecture is a characteristic sign of a restless student.

form_sentences.sentence: His laughter was more characteristic of his father than of anyone else in the family.
Her strong character helped her cope with the hardships of the job.
Characteristically, he arrived late to the meeting, without any apology.

definition: The amount of money that someone must pay for a product or service.
extra_senses: to make a rush at or sudden attack upon, as in battle
(criminal law) a pleading describing some wrong or offense
examples: The shop charged a small fee for delivering the furniture to our flat.
There is no charge for parking at the hospital on Friday mornings.
The bank added a service charge to my account after I withdrew cash.
The hotel's charge for breakfast was higher than we expected.
Please ask the driver about the charge for the airport trip before you get in.

form_sentences.sentence: Please pack a phone charger, because the hostel has only two plugs.

definition: A special personal quality that makes other people admire you and want to follow you.
examples: The new class captain has so much charisma that even shy students follow her ideas.
A good salesperson needs more than product knowledge; a little charisma helps customers trust you.
He is not the best singer, but his charisma on stage keeps the audience clapping.
Online video creators often rely on charisma rather than expensive equipment to win followers.
My grandfather’s quiet charisma made everyone in the neighborhood come to him for advice.

form_sentences.sentence: The charismatic coach inspired the team to train harder every single day.

definition: An organisation that helps people in need, or the act of giving help and money to them.
extra_senses: a kindly and lenient attitude toward people
an activity or gift that benefits the public at large
examples: My aunt volunteers at a charity that provides meals to poor families.
Many students collect old books and give them to a local charity.
The mosque committee raised money for flood relief through a charity drive.
Our class ran a bake sale to support a children's charity in the district.
Donating a small amount to charity can make a real difference to someone's life.

form_sentences.sentence: Several charities distributed food and blankets to families after the flood.

definition: A person who pretends to have special skills or knowledge, usually to cheat people out of money.
examples: The so-called healer was a charlatan who sold colored water as a cure for every illness.
Do not trust any charlatan who promises that you will pass the exam without studying.
The investment adviser turned out to be a charlatan who vanished with his clients' savings.
A charlatan in the village sold fake gold chains to families before the wedding season.
He called himself a business guru, but his clients soon decided he was a charlatan.

form_sentences.sentence: Many charlatans sell fake cures online, so always check reviews from trusted sources.

definition: A drawing, table or diagram that shows information clearly, often using lines, bars or symbols.
extra_senses: make a chart of
a map designed to assist navigation by air or sea
examples: The bar chart shows how much rain fell in each month of the monsoon.
The nurse hung the temperature chart at the end of the patient's bed.
We drew a pie chart to show how the class spends its pocket money.
A wall chart with all the verb tenses helped me prepare for the English test.
The sales chart on the manager's screen made it clear that profits had fallen.

definition: To run after someone or something in order to catch or reach them.
extra_senses: the act of pursuing in an effort to overtake or capture
United States politician and jurist who served as chief justice of the United States Supreme Court (1808-1873)
examples: The stray dog began to chase the cat across the empty car park.
The police chased the thief through the narrow lanes of the old town.
Our little brother likes to chase pigeons near the mosque steps.
After the bus left, I had to run and chase it for two blocks.
She decided to chase her dream of becoming a doctor despite the long study hours.

form_sentences.sentence: The dog has chased the cat up the tree again.
The boys are chasing a kite across the open field.
Chasing a dream takes courage, but it can change your life.
The little girl chases her younger brother around the garden every afternoon.

definition: To force someone or something to leave a place, often by pursuing or frightening them.
examples: My grandmother chased the crows away from the rice she had laid out to dry.
The guard chased away the boys who were climbing over the school wall.
A loud thunderclap chased the cows away from the open field.
Strong coffee chased away the sleepiness I felt during the morning lecture.
Please chase those mosquitoes away before we start the evening prayers.

form_sentences.sentence: The farmers have chased away the monkeys from the mango trees.
The security guard is chasing away loiterers from the school gate.
Chasing away birds from the rice field takes patience and early mornings.
The loud horn of the rickshaw chases away the stray dogs on the road.
Use a loud whistle to chase away wild animals on the farm.

definition: A very deep, wide gap in the ground; also, a serious gap between two groups or ideas.
examples: After the earthquake, a wide chasm opened across the road, and cars could not pass.
The hikers crossed the deep chasm on a narrow wooden bridge.
Rocks tumbled into the dark chasm, and we never heard them hit the bottom.
The explorers lowered ropes into the chasm to study the caves below.
A chasm separated the two brothers' views about selling the family land.
collocations: a chasm between A and B

form_sentences.sentence: Deep chasms split the mountain range, making the journey dangerous for hikers.

definition: Simple and plain in style, or morally pure and avoiding sexual activity.
extra_senses: pure and simple in design or style
abstaining from unlawful sexual intercourse
examples: The room had a chaste white design, with no pictures and almost no furniture.
The poet praised the chaste beauty of the snow-covered hills.
The couple exchanged a chaste kiss on the cheek at the railway station.
The architect admired the chaste lines of the old library, which had no carvings at all.
The old novel presents love as a chaste and respectful friendship.

form_sentences.sentence: The poem's language seemed chaste, plain and simple, without any decoration.
The design of the new office is more chaste than the old one, with fewer decorations.
The monk's vow of chastity shaped every part of his daily life.

definition: To scold or criticize someone severely for doing something wrong.

form_sentences.sentence: The old refrigerator has consumed far more electricity than the new one.
The town's growing population is consuming water faster than the wells can refill.
Consuming too much sugar can increase the risk of diabetes.
The new laptop is designed to consume less energy than older models.

definition: A person who buys and uses goods or services for their own personal needs.
examples: Consumers in the city complained when the price of cooking gas suddenly doubled.
As a careful consumer, my mother always compares prices before buying medicine.
Consumer rights groups warned shoppers to check expiry dates on imported biscuits.
The company launched a new app to help consumers track their electricity bills.
Every consumer has the right to a refund if the product they bought is faulty.

form_sentences.sentence: Doctors advise people to consume less sugar and more vegetables.

definition: Having or showing the highest level of skill; perfect or complete in every way.
extra_senses: make perfect; bring to perfection
having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
examples: The chef is a consummate professional who never loses his calm, even when the restaurant is full.
She handled the angry crowd with consummate skill and sent everyone home smiling.
He is a consummate storyteller, and his grandchildren listen in silence for hours.
The pilot landed the plane in strong wind with consummate ease.
Her consummate attention to detail impressed the interview panel.

form_sentences.sentence: The chef seems consummate in every detail, from the plating to the sauce.
Her acting was more consummate in the second act than in the first.
The signing ceremony marked the consummation of months of careful planning.

definition: Communication with someone, or a situation in which you meet, speak to or touch them.
extra_senses: be in or establish communication with
the act of touching physically
examples: I lost contact with my school friends after we moved to different cities.
Contact with the village was cut off for two days after the flood.
Please keep in contact with the office while you are traveling.
Doctors advise people with the flu to avoid close contact with others.
Eye contact is important during an interview because it shows confidence.

definition: To have something inside it, or to include something as one of its parts.
extra_senses: contain or hold; have within
lessen the intensity of; temper; hold in restraint; hold or keep within limits
examples: The small box can contain three kilograms of rice, so do not overfill it.
Each packet of biscuits contains a sachet of dried mango powder for flavour.
This bottle contains cough syrup, so keep it away from small children.
The old wooden trunk contains letters and photographs from my grandfather's youth.
The report contains detailed figures about the spread of the dengue outbreak.
example_usage: Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The box contained old letters and a few faded photographs.
The parcel has contained some broken glass, so handle it carefully.
The bottle is containing a mixture of water and salt for the experiment.
Containing the spread of the virus needs both care and cooperation.

definition: An object such as a box, jar or bottle that is used to hold or store things.
examples: We stored the spices in a glass container with a tight lid to keep them fresh.
The shipping container arrived at the port with imported machinery inside.
Please wash the plastic container well before filling it with leftover biryani.
The street vendor kept the tea in a large steel container under his umbrella.
A big container truck blocked the narrow road near the market this morning.

form_sentences.sentence: Store the leftover curry in clean containers and keep them in the fridge.
This jar can contain about one litre of milk.

definition: Belonging to the present time; modern.
extra_senses: belonging to the present time
a person of nearly the same age as another
examples: The museum has an exhibition of contemporary art by young artists from Dhaka.
The shop sells contemporary furniture with simple lines and light colors.
Many contemporary writers publish their stories online before printing them as books.
The novel deals with contemporary problems such as unemployment and rising rent.
Contemporary architecture often uses glass and steel to let in more light.

form_sentences.sentence: The museum's design feels contemporary, with glass walls and open spaces.
Compared with the old tunes, the band's latest songs sound more contemporary.

definition: A strong feeling of disrespect for someone or something that you think is worthless.
extra_senses: a manner that is generally disrespectful and contemptuous
open disrespect for a person or thing
examples: She looked at the cheating player with contempt and refused to shake his hand.
Many fans felt only contempt for the club’s owner after he sold the best players.
He holds the traffic rules in contempt, driving through red lights without a thought.
The judge warned that anyone who showed contempt for the court would be removed.
The review treated the new novel with open contempt, calling it empty and boring.

form_sentences.sentence: He gave a contemptuous look at the cheap phone on the table.

definition: Deserving no respect because of being very bad, dishonest or cowardly.
examples: Stealing money from a charity box is a contemptible act.
I found his decision to blame the cleaner for his own mistake contemptible.
The newspaper called the scam a contemptible trick played on the elderly.
Spreading rumors about a classmate's family is contemptible behavior.
He felt contemptible after lying to his best friend.

form_sentences.sentence: Stealing from a sick neighbor is more contemptible than simple carelessness.
The manager contemptibly blamed the new staff for the company's mistake.

definition: The things that a container or document holds, or the subject that a book, talk or film deals with.
extra_senses: what a communication that is about something is about
satisfy in a limited way
examples: The content of the lecture was useful, but the teacher spoke far too quickly.
Before you buy the book, read the content list to check which chapters it covers.
The website's content is updated every morning with the latest news for students.
I liked the content of the film, although the ending seemed a little rushed.
The content of the box was mostly old newspapers and a few broken toys.

form_sentences.sentence: The contentment on his face showed he was happy with the result.
Each package can contain a short guide and a sample test.
The contented customers left the shop with big smiles on their faces.

definition: An opinion or point that someone states and argues for as true.
extra_senses: a contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement
the act of competing as for profit or a prize
examples: It is my contention that students learn better when school starts later in the morning.
The lawyer's main contention was that her client was out of town that night.
Scientists studied the data and found little to support his contention.
Her contention that the new bus route would save time turned out to be correct.
The report rejects the contention that online classes are less effective than classroom lessons.

form_sentences.sentence: Their contentions about the budget were discussed at the meeting.
Several students contend that the exam was too long this year.
The contentious topic of the debate divided the audience into two groups.

definition: Likely to cause arguments, or always ready to argue.
extra_senses: involving or likely to cause controversy
examples: The plan to close the old market became a contentious issue in the neighborhood.
My contentious cousin argues about everything, from football scores to the price of tea.
Dividing the family land was a contentious matter that took years to settle.
The meeting turned contentious when two committee members disagreed about the budget.
Avoid contentious topics at the dinner table if you want a peaceful evening.

form_sentences.sentence: The question of fees was more contentious than the rest of the meeting.
The contentiousness of the new parking rules split the neighborhood in two.

definition: An event in which people or teams compete to win a prize, title or victory.
extra_senses: to make the subject of dispute, contention, or litigation
a struggle between rivals
examples: Our school held a spelling contest, and my younger sister won the first prize.
Three teams entered the chess contest at the university hall this weekend.
The national football contest is broadcast live on television every year.
She lost the local election contest by a few hundred votes after a close count.
The quiz contest was fierce, and the winners were announced after midnight.

form_sentences.sentence: The school holds several essay contests during the year.

definition: A person who takes part in a competition, quiz or contest.
extra_senses: a person who dissents from some established policy
examples: Each contestant in the spelling bee had two minutes to answer.
The youngest contestant in the cooking show was only twelve years old.
A nervous contestant forgot the answer, and the whole audience whispered hints.
Every contestant received a certificate for taking part in the school quiz.
Contestants must register online before the deadline to enter the photography contest.

definition: The situation, background or surrounding words that help explain the meaning of something.
extra_senses: the set of facts or circumstances that surround a situation or event
examples: You can often guess a new word's meaning from the context of the sentence.
The news report gave no context, so many readers misunderstood the figures.
In a business context, arriving on time is a basic sign of respect.
Without context, that text message looks rude, but she was only joking.
The museum guide explained the historical context of the old fort, which made the visit far more interesting.

form_sentences.sentence: Students should practise new words in several contexts, not just from lists.
Use contextual clues, such as nearby words, to guess a word's meaning.

definition: To describe or consider something together with the background or circumstances that help explain it.
examples: The teacher contextualized the poem by explaining the time and place in which it was written.
News reports should contextualize crime figures by comparing them with earlier years.
To understand the old slang, you need to contextualize it within the culture of its time.
Before judging his quote, let us contextualize it by reading the whole speech.
The museum guide contextualized each object with a short story about its owner.
example_usage: Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The report has been contextualized with figures from the last decade.
The lecturer is contextualizing the poem within the history of the period.
Contextualizing the data helps readers understand why the numbers changed.
The introduction contextualizes the novel for students who are new to it.

definition: Sharing a border or touching; next to one another without a gap.
extra_senses: connecting without a break; within a common boundary
having a common boundary or edge; abutting; touching
examples: Bangladesh is contiguous with India along most of its border.
The two rooms are contiguous, so we opened the folding door and made one big hall.
Our house is contiguous to the school playground, so we hear the children all morning.
The farmer bought two contiguous plots of land so that he could dig a single large pond.
A contiguous stretch of forest is better for wildlife than small, scattered patches.

definition: One of the seven very large areas of land on the earth, such as Asia or Africa.
extra_senses: the European mainland
having control over urination and defecation
examples: Asia is the largest continent on the earth and holds more than half the world's people.
Bangladesh lies in South Asia, which is part of the continent of Asia.
Geography lessons taught us the names of every continent and the major oceans.
Many workers from our country travel to other continents in search of jobs.
The explorer spent years crossing the continent in search of new trade routes.

form_sentences.sentence: Scientists study how continental plates move slowly over millions of years.

definition: Depending on something else that may or may not happen.
extra_senses: possible but not certain to occur
a temporary military unit
examples: Our picnic is contingent on the weather, so we will decide on Friday.
The job offer is contingent upon passing a medical check.
Her scholarship is contingent on keeping her marks above eighty percent.
Everything about the plan is contingent, so we must stay flexible.
Whether we travel to Cox's Bazar is contingent on the bus tickets being available.

form_sentences.sentence: We made a contingent plan in case the bus was late.
The success of the project is more contingent on funding than on the team's effort.
Every good traveller keeps a contingency fund for unexpected costs and delays.

definition: To keep doing something without stopping, or to go on again after a pause or interruption.
extra_senses: continue talking
keep or maintain in unaltered condition; cause to remain or last
examples: After the short break, the teacher asked us to continue reading the next chapter.
The rain may continue through the night, so carry an umbrella tomorrow morning.
If the bus is still late, we will continue our journey by rickshaw.
The farmers continued to work in the paddy field despite the scorching heat.
My grandmother continues to make her famous sweet rice every Eid morning.
example_usage: Base form · after a modal or auxiliary
Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The rain has continued since morning, so the match was postponed.
The bus service is continuing on the highway despite the road works.
Continuing to study after a long day takes real discipline.
The continuation of the lecture series will start next Monday.

definition: Going on without any stop, break or gap in time or in space.
extra_senses: of a function or curve; extending without break or irregularity
examples: The machines in the factory run in a continuous cycle day and night without stopping.
There was a continuous power cut in the village for two days after the storm.
The children heard a continuous buzzing sound from the broken electric fan.
She has made continuous progress since she started learning English last year.
The city's water supply should be continuous, but in some areas it stops often.

form_sentences.sentence: The rain was more continuous in the afternoon than in the morning.
The skills of students form a continuum from beginner to expert.
The fan has been running continuously since morning, so it is hot.

definition: Without any stop or gap, or happening all the time in an unbroken way.
extra_senses: with unflagging resolve
examples: The phone rang continuously during the wedding, so my uncle switched it off.
The generator has been running continuously since the power went off at dawn.
The students read continuously for three hours before taking a short break.
Rain fell continuously over the village, and the river rose higher each day.
The guard watched the gate continuously, so no unknown visitor could enter.

form_sentences.sentence: A continuous supply of electricity is important for the hospital.

definition: A continuous series in which neighbouring parts are barely different, though the two ends are very different.
examples: Teachers see reading ability as a continuum, not a simple choice between good and poor.
Shy and outgoing are two ends of a continuum, and most people sit somewhere in the middle.
The colours of the rainbow form a continuum, with no clear line where red becomes orange.
Health is better seen as a continuum from poor to excellent than as a choice between sick and well.
Our shop's customers range along a continuum from casual buyers to loyal regulars.

form_sentences.sentence: Mood and energy are best seen as continuums rather than simple on-or-off switches.
The rain was continuous all night, so the streets were flooded by morning.

definition: Goods that are brought into or taken out of a country illegally, or that are forbidden by law.
extra_senses: goods whose importation or exportation or possession is prohibited by law
examples: Customs officers seized a large amount of contraband hidden inside a truck full of vegetables.
Mobile phones are treated as contraband in some prisons.
The border guards arrested two men for carrying contraband across the river at night.
At the airport, dogs are trained to sniff out contraband such as illegal drugs.
The exam hall rules say that any contraband, like notes or smart watches, will be taken away.

definition: A written agreement between people or companies that is legally binding.
extra_senses: enter into a contractual arrangement
engage by written agreement
examples: Read the rental contract carefully before you pay the deposit for the flat.
The builder broke the contract by using cheaper bricks than we had agreed on.
She got a six-month contract at a design firm after her final exams.
The farmer signed a contract to sell his entire potato harvest to a food company at a fixed price.
The mobile phone contract includes twenty gigabytes of data and unlimited calls at night.

form_sentences.sentence: Please read the contractual terms carefully before you sign.
The contractor finished painting the classroom walls two days early.

definition: To say that something someone said is wrong, or to be so different from something that both cannot be true.
extra_senses: deny the truth of
be resistant to
examples: It is rude to contradict your teacher in front of the whole class.
The two witnesses contradicted each other about what time the accident happened.
The new research contradicts the old belief that sugar makes children hyperactive.
Your actions contradict your words: you say you love books but never read one.
The map contradicted the signboard, so we asked a passerby for directions.

form_sentences.sentence: Her new evidence has contradicted the earlier witness statement.
The latest study is contradicting an old belief about breakfast.
Contradicting your boss in a meeting needs care and respect.
The two reports gave contradictory figures for the same month's rainfall.
There is a contradiction between the menu and the price list.

definition: Two things or ideas that are exact opposites of each other.
examples: Hot and cold are contraries, so a drink cannot be both at the same time.
My twin brothers are contraries: one is loud and sporty, the other quiet and bookish.
Courage and fear are not always contraries, since a brave person can feel afraid and still act.
Dhaka is a city of contraries, where glass towers stand near crowded lanes full of rickshaws.
In the debate, the two speakers presented contraries, and the judges had to decide which view was stronger.
collocations: contraries such as hot and cold

definition: Completely different or opposite in nature, direction or meaning.
extra_senses: a relation of direct opposition
of words or propositions so related that both cannot be true but both may be false
examples: Contrary to what many students believe, studying all night usually lowers your exam score.
Her contrary opinion surprised the committee, which had expected her to agree.
The manager took the contrary view and argued that the project should be delayed.
We had to turn back because contrary winds kept pushing the boat away from the shore.
The test results were contrary to the doctor's first guess.

form_sentences.sentence: My brother becomes more contrary whenever someone tells him what to do.
His contrariness made every group discussion longer than it needed to be.

definition: A clear difference between two or more things that are compared.
extra_senses: the act of distinguishing by comparing differences
put in opposition to show or emphasize differences
examples: There is a sharp contrast between life in the city and life in the village.
In contrast to her quiet sister, Maya loves speaking in front of crowds.
The bright red door makes a strong contrast with the white wall.
The teacher asked us to write about the contrast between the two characters.
The warm weather today is a welcome contrast to last week's cold rain.

definition: Clearly different from something else, so that the two stand out when placed side by side.
examples: The two paintings have contrasting colours, one very dark and the other very bright.
The brothers have contrasting personalities: one is shy and the other is outgoing.
The article presents contrasting views on whether the new road will help farmers.
Their contrasting approaches to studying led to very different results in the exam.
The design uses contrasting shades of green and white to make the sign stand out.

form_sentences.sentence: The two designs are contrasting in style, so the client had a clear choice.
The colours of the two saris are more contrasting than I expected.
The teacher asked us to contrast the two poems in our essay.
There is a sharp contrast between the quiet morning and the noisy evening in Dhaka.

definition: To break a law, rule or agreement.
extra_senses: deny the truth of
examples: Drivers who park here contravene the city's traffic rules.
The factory contravened safety regulations and was fined.
Copying answers from a friend contravenes the school's exam rules.
The advertisement contravened the law by making false health claims.
Selling medicine without a license contravenes the pharmacy regulations.

form_sentences.sentence: The company has contravened the safety rules and must pay a fine.
The shop is contravening the city's noise rules after midnight.
Contravening the building code can make a house unsafe for families.
Nobody should dare to contravene the exam rules by using a phone.
Any contravention of the hostel curfew will lead to a warning.

definition: A small, unexpected and embarrassing disagreement or mishap, especially in public.
examples: We had a small contretemps at the restaurant when two bills arrived for one table.
A contretemps over seat numbers delayed the start of the show.
A contretemps with a stuck door left the groom late for his own ceremony.
Her contretemps with the bank clerk ended when he found the missing form.
The wedding photographer had an awkward contretemps with the caterer over table space.

definition: To give something, such as money, time or ideas, to help achieve something together with others.
extra_senses: contribute to some cause
be conducive to
examples: Every student contributed fifty taka to buy flowers for our retiring teacher.
Rafi contributed several good ideas during the team meeting.
Neighbors contributed food and blankets after the fire destroyed several homes.
She contributes a small part of her salary to a local charity every month.
Everyone in the group contributed to the final report.

form_sentences.sentence: Many volunteers have contributed their time to the flood relief camp.
Several students are contributing ideas to the school magazine this year.
Contributing to a savings account every month builds financial security.
She wants to contribute more to the team by sharing useful research.
The class captain's contribution made the reunion party a big success.

definition: Something a person gives or does to help achieve a result, such as money, time or ideas.
extra_senses: a voluntary gift (as of money or service or ideas) made to some worthwhile cause
act of giving in common with others for a common purpose especially to a charity
examples: Every family in the colony made a contribution to the fund for the flood victims.
Her contribution to the school magazine earned praise from the headmaster.
My father's contribution to the project was the careful planning of the budget.
The club welcomed the contribution of new ideas from its younger members.
A generous contribution from a local businessman helped build the new library.

form_sentences.sentence: Each member made small contributions to the school fund this year.
Every student can contribute ideas to the group project.

definition: Feeling or showing deep regret for having done something wrong.
examples: He looked contrite when he admitted that he had broken his sister's tablet.
The contrite driver apologized to the shopkeeper and offered to pay for the damaged cart.
She wrote a contrite email to her teacher after submitting the assignment late.
A contrite smile crossed Nadia's face when she realized she had forgotten her friend's birthday.
The company issued a contrite statement after the data leak and promised to improve security.

form_sentences.sentence: He looked more contrite after apologising to his teacher.
She contritely admitted that she had copied the homework from her friend.

definition: To plan or make something cleverly, often using skill and effort in a difficult situation.
extra_senses: come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
put or send forth
examples: Using old bottles and tape, the students contrived a simple water filter for the science fair.
She contrived a way to attend both events by leaving the first one early.
The two friends contrived to meet outside the cinema without their parents noticing.
During load-shedding, my father contrived a reading lamp from a phone torch and a glass of water.
The hungry travellers contrived a meal from a few biscuits and some tea.

form_sentences.sentence: The villagers have contrived a clever way to store water during the dry season.
Our neighbors are contriving a plan to share the rooftop garden.
Contriving an excuse at the last minute made the situation worse.
The writer contrives a surprising twist that keeps readers guessing.
The engineer had to contrive a temporary fix before the flood arrived.

definition: Not natural or spontaneous; obviously planned or forced in order to produce an effect.
extra_senses: artificially formal
examples: The movie's ending felt contrived, as if the writer had run out of ideas.
Her contrived excuse about a sick cat did not fool the teacher.
The interview question seemed contrived to make candidates look foolish.
Their contrived laughter at the boss's joke made the room feel awkward.
The reality show's conflicts were so contrived that viewers stopped believing them.

form_sentences.sentence: The ending of the film felt more contrived than the rest of the story.

definition: To direct, manage or limit how something behaves or develops, so that it stays as you want.
extra_senses: lessen the intensity of; temper; hold in restraint; hold or keep within limits
power to direct or determine
examples: The teacher controlled the noisy class by speaking firmly and calmly.
Please control your spending so that you can save for the university fees.
The police tried to control the crowd outside the stadium after the match.
The government announced new measures to control the rising price of onions.
My mother controlled the sugar in the tea so that my father would not complain.

form_sentences.sentence: The doctor has controlled my blood pressure with a simple daily tablet.
The traffic police are controlling the crowd near the station.
Controlling your spending is the key to saving money each month.
The teacher controls the volume of the class with a gentle signal.
The air traffic controller guided the plane safely to the runway.

definition: Carefully managed and kept within limits, so that it does not get out of hand.
examples: The factory keeps the vaccines in a controlled temperature room to stay safe.
She spoke in a calm, controlled voice even though she was very angry.
The patient's blood sugar has remained controlled since he began the new diet.
The experiment was carried out in a controlled environment to avoid errors.
Only a few people have access to the controlled area of the hospital.

form_sentences.sentence: The second speech was more controlled than the first, with fewer pauses.

definition: A long public argument or disagreement about something that many people feel strongly about.
examples: The new school uniform rule caused a lot of controversy among parents.
There is still controversy over whether homework helps young children learn.
A careless comment by a football coach sparked controversy on social media yesterday.
The decision to cut down the old trees in the park led to public controversy.
The controversy over the exam results ended when the board published the corrected marks.

form_sentences.sentence: The film festival has faced several controversies over its selection of movies.
The shop owner decided to contest the fine in court.
The new school uniform rule remains controversial among parents and students.

definition: Stubbornly refusing to obey authority or follow rules.
examples: The contumacious student ignored every warning and kept using his phone in class.
The court fined the contumacious witness for refusing to answer the judge's questions.
My contumacious little brother refuses to wear a helmet, no matter how often Dad insists.
A contumacious employee who ignores safety rules can put the whole team at risk.
The patient was contumacious about the doctor's advice and went back to eating oily food every day.

form_sentences.sentence: The stubborn student became more contumacious after every warning from the principal.

definition: Stubborn refusal to obey or accept authority, especially an order from a court.
extra_senses: obstinate rebelliousness and insubordination; resistance to authority
examples: The witness was fined for contumacy after ignoring three court summonses.
The committee grew tired of the member's contumacy and finally cancelled his membership.
An old legal textbook describes contumacy as a refusal to attend a hearing.
The student's contumacy, shown by tearing up the warning letter, led to his suspension.
His contumacy toward every rule at the hostel finally forced the warden to call his father.

definition: Rude and insulting words or behaviour that show a lack of respect.
examples: The prisoner was treated with contumely by the guards, who laughed at him.
She endured the contumely of her classmates for months because she wore old clothes.
Honest workers should not have to face contumely from rude customers.
The newspaper's contumely towards the actor shocked many readers.
He replied to the polite request with contumely, calling the staff useless and lazy.

definition: A confusing and difficult problem or question.
examples: How to pay for university without a loan is a conundrum for many families.
The missing keys were a real conundrum: we had searched every room twice.
Choosing between a well-paid job and a happy one is a conundrum many graduates face.
The teacher gave the class a conundrum: how can you divide five apples equally among six people?
Why the old clock stopped at exactly midnight each day remains a conundrum.

form_sentences.sentence: Students face many conundrums when choosing between two good universities.

definition: To come together for a meeting, or to call people together for one.
extra_senses: call together
examples: The principal convened a meeting of all teachers to discuss the exam schedule.
The committee will convene at ten o'clock tomorrow in the conference room.
Family members convened at my grandmother's house for Eid lunch.
Doctors from across the country convened in Dhaka for a conference on heart disease.
The class representative convened the students to plan the farewell party.
example_usage: Base form · after a modal or auxiliary

form_sentences.sentence: The board has convened an emergency meeting to discuss the funding problem.
The class captain is convening everyone in the hall after lunch for a quick talk.
Convening a meeting on short notice is hard when people are busy.
The head teacher convenes the staff every Monday to review the week's plans.
The annual convention brought together teachers from every district in the country.

definition: Easy to use or reach, and saving you time or trouble.
extra_senses: large and roomy (`convenient' is archaic in this sense)
examples: Our apartment is convenient for work because the bus stop is right outside.
Would Thursday afternoon be a convenient time for the meeting?
Mobile banking is convenient because you can pay bills without standing in line.
A flask of hot water is a convenient way to make tea during a long journey.
The pharmacy opens late, which is convenient for people who work long hours.

form_sentences.sentence: The new bus stop is more convenient for students living near the market.
The convenience of online banking saves hours of waiting in queues.
The hostel is conveniently located near the bus station and the library.

definition: A way of behaving or doing something that most people in a society accept as normal or correct.
extra_senses: something regarded as a normative example
(diplomacy) an international agreement
examples: In our family, it is a convention to greet the elders first.
By convention, the host serves the guests before eating.
The artist ignored convention and painted the sky green.
Writing the date at the top of a letter is a long-standing convention.
Dress conventions at the office are more relaxed on Fridays.

form_sentences.sentence: Her conventional approach to teaching worked well for most students.
The board will convene next Monday to review the new admission rules.

definition: Following the usual, accepted way of doing things, rather than being new or unusual.
extra_senses: conforming with accepted standards
(weapons) using energy for propulsion or destruction that is not nuclear energy
examples: My parents hoped I would choose a conventional career, such as medicine or engineering.
The restaurant serves only conventional dishes, with nothing unusual on the menu.
Conventional wisdom says you should save part of every paycheck.
She wore a conventional black suit to the job interview.
Some farmers prefer conventional methods to new machines they cannot afford.

form_sentences.sentence: Her wedding plans seemed conventional, with the usual songs and flowers.
His cooking became more conventional after he returned to the family kitchen.
The conventionality of the design disappointed the young architects.
She dressed conventionally for the interview in a plain grey suit.

definition: To move toward the same point and meet there, or to become similar or joined.
extra_senses: approach a limit as the number of terms increases without limit
move or draw together at a certain location
examples: Fans from all over the city converged on the stadium before the final match.
The two rivers converge near the town and flow on as one wide stream.
The two lines on the graph converge at the point where supply meets demand.
Our opinions began to converge once we had shared all the facts.
On Eid eve, relatives converged on the village from every direction.

form_sentences.sentence: The two roads have converged near the old bus terminal in Gulshan.
Hundreds of students are converging on the campus for the entrance exam.
Converging on one answer took the team two long meetings.
The river converges with a smaller stream just outside the village.
Convergent evidence from three studies strengthened the researchers' conclusion.

definition: Familiar with a subject or skill because you have learned about it or used it.
examples: The new teacher is conversant with the latest software for online classes.
You should be conversant with the exam format before test day.
My grandfather is not conversant with smartphones, so he asks me for help.

definition: A table with drawers or shelves, used for writing, studying, or working at.
examples: My younger brother does his homework at a small desk beside the bedroom window.

definition: Extremely worried and ready to try anything because your situation is very bad.
extra_senses: desperately determined
a person who is frightened and in need of help

In a desperate attempt to finish on time, the students worked through the night.

form_sentences.sentence: The family became more desperate after the flood destroyed their home.

ipa: /ˈdɛs pər ət li, ˈdɛ sprət li/
definition: Very urgently, or with extreme need, hope, or fear.
extra_senses: in intense despair
examples: The family desperately needed clean drinking water after the flood damaged their well.

form_sentences.sentence: The desperate farmer searched for water after the long dry spell.

definition: To feel strong dislike and disrespect for someone or something you think is unworthy.
examples: Nadia despises cheating, so she refused to share her answers during the admission test.
Commuters in Dhaka despise the long traffic jams that waste hours of their day.
The staff secretly despised their manager because he took credit for their hard work.
My grandmother despises wasting food, so she saves every leftover grain of rice.
Many readers despise online scams that trick elderly people out of their savings.

form_sentences.sentence: The villagers have despised the greedy landlord for many years.
Our neighbor is despising the noisy construction work next door.

definition: Used to show that something happens or is true although something else might have prevented it.
extra_senses: contemptuous disregard
examples: Despite the heavy rain, thousands of fans waited outside the stadium.
She passed the exam despite studying for only two weeks.

definition: Very sad and without hope, usually because of failure or disappointment.
examples: After failing the admission test twice, Rafi felt despondent and stopped studying for weeks.

definition: A ruler who has total power and uses it cruelly and unfairly.
examples: The history book describes a despot who taxed farmers until they had no food.
The people celebrated when the old despot finally lost power.

A good manager is a leader, not a despot who demands blind obedience.
The novel's villain is a despot who punishes anyone who laughs at him.

form_sentences.sentence: Historians describe several despots who ruled with cruelty and fear.

definition: Having no money, food or possessions; extremely poor.
extra_senses: completely wanting or lacking
examples: The flood left hundreds of families destitute, without homes, food or clothes.

The charity runs a shelter for destitute children who live on the streets.

Once a rich merchant, he died destitute and alone in a rented room.

form_sentences.sentence: After the flood, the families became more destitute with every passing week.

extra_senses: destroy completely; damage irreparably

a final state

definition: Lacking a plan or purpose, and done without enthusiasm or steady effort.

form_sentences.sentence: His attempts to revise grammar became more desultory as the week went on.

definition: Not emotionally involved, so that you seem calm, objective or distant.
extra_senses: being or feeling set or kept apart from others
no longer connected or joined
examples: The doctor spoke in a calm, detached voice while explaining the test results.

His detached manner made the customers think he was not interested in helping.

form_sentences.sentence: After a few months at the new job, she became more detached from the gossip.

definition: A small piece of information, or a single feature, that is part of something larger.

extended treatment of particulars
examples: Please check the small details in the contract before you sign it on Monday.

definition: Including a lot of precise information and small particulars.
examples: The engineer prepared a detailed report on the condition of the bridge after the flood.

definition: To notice or discover something that is hard to see, hear or feel.
examples: The smoke alarm detected the smoke and woke everyone in the building.
Doctors can now detect many diseases at an early stage with simple blood tests.

Airport scanners can detect metal objects hidden inside passengers' bags.
The software will detect spelling errors and underline them in red.

definition: The quality of being firmly committed to doing something, despite difficulties.
extra_senses: the quality of being determined to do or achieve something; firmness of purpose
a position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration
examples: Her determination to pass the exam helped her study every night for six months.

definition: To find out or decide something exactly, after investigation or calculation.
extra_senses: shape or influence; give direction to
fix conclusively or authoritatively
examples: The doctors are trying to determine the cause of the fever that is spreading in the area.

definition: Having a firm intention to do something, and refusing to give up.
extra_senses: having been learned or found or determined especially by investigation
devoting full strength and concentrated attention to

definition: Something that discourages people from doing something, especially by making them afraid of the results.

definition: To gradually grow, or to make something grow, larger, better, or more advanced.

definition: Different in an unusual way from what is normal, expected or accepted.

definition: A small machine or tool made for a particular purpose, especially an electronic one.

definition: Great love, loyalty or commitment shown to a person, cause or activity.

definition: Deeply religious and committed to the practices of your faith.

definition: Skilful and quick, especially in the way you use your hands.

definition: Skilled at using your hands, or quick and clever in the way you handle things.

form_sentences.sentence: The announcer has enunciated every word clearly for the live audience.
Our drama teacher is enunciating each line slowly for the new students.
Enunciating clearly is important when you give a speech in a large hall.
Her clear enunciation made the radio news easy to follow.

definition: A flat paper cover, usually rectangular, that is used to hold a letter or card.
extra_senses: any wrapper or covering
a curve that is tangent to each of a family of curves
examples: I sealed the envelope and wrote my cousin's address carefully in blue ink.
The wedding invitation came in a red envelope with gold letters on the front.
Please put the stamp on the envelope before you post it at the post office.
The bank sent my monthly statement in a plain white envelope.
Inside the envelope was an exam result, and my heart beat fast as I opened it.

form_sentences.sentence: She sealed the wedding invitations into small cream envelopes and posted them.

definition: The natural world, or the surroundings in which a person lives, works or learns.
extra_senses: the area in which something exists or lives
examples: Plastic bags are bad for the environment because they take hundreds of years to break down.
A quiet library is the best environment for students who need to concentrate.
Our office has a friendly working environment, and colleagues help each other during busy weeks.
Frogs and fish cannot survive when their natural environment is polluted.
Babies usually sleep better in a dark, quiet environment.

form_sentences.sentence: Students learn better in calm environments with good light and fresh air.
Environmental pollution from factories is a serious concern in many large cities.

definition: Relating to the natural world, its protection, or the effects of human activity on it.
extra_senses: concerned with the ecological effects of altering the environment
examples: Plastic bags cause serious environmental damage because they take years to break down.
Our school club organizes an environmental clean-up on the beach every winter.
The new factory must follow strict environmental rules before it can open.
Using public transport reduces the environmental impact of traffic in big cities.
Her environmental research studied how polluted water affects fish in the river.

form_sentences.sentence: The pollution in the lake is clearly environmental, so the city must act now.
Paper bags are more environmental than plastic ones, though they cost more.
A clean environment helps children learn better and stay healthy.
The school is environmentally responsible, using rainwater for the gardens.

definition: To picture something in your mind as a future possibility, especially something you hope will happen.
extra_senses: picture to oneself; imagine possible
examples: Before opening the shop, Nadia tried to envision how customers would move between the shelves.
I can't envision myself living abroad, away from my family and our daily evening tea.
The architect envisions a public park with a small lake where the old factory now stands.
Few people could have envisioned how deeply smartphones would change the way we study.
Our coach envisions a team that trains together daily and supports each other off the field.

form_sentences.sentence: The young architect envisioned a park with bamboo bridges above the lake.
The team is envisioning a faster train link between Dhaka and Chattogram.
Envisioning your future career early can help you choose the right courses.
The envisioning of a smart city helped the council plan new roads and parks.

definition: Lasting for a very short time.
extra_senses: anything short-lived, as an insect that lives only for a day in its winged form
examples: Fame on social media can be ephemeral, lasting only until the next trend appears.
The beauty of shiuli flowers is ephemeral; they bloom at night and fall by morning.
Morning dew is ephemeral and vanishes as soon as the sun rises.
Many fashion trends are ephemeral, so spending a lot of money on them is unwise.
Some chat apps send ephemeral messages that disappear a few seconds after they are read.

form_sentences.sentence: The ephemeral joy of the festival faded when the lights went out.
Social media trends are more ephemeral than the songs of the past.
Collectors value old ephemera, such as tickets and posters.

definition: A person who enjoys fine food and drink and knows a lot about it.
examples: My uncle is an epicure who travels across the country just to taste a famous kacchi biryani.
