definition: Not clear or exact; lacking detail so that the meaning or shape is hard to see.
extra_senses: not precisely limited, determined, or distinguished
lacking clarity or distinctness

form_sentences.sentence: His second answer was vaguer than the first, so I still did not understand.

definition: Legally or officially acceptable, or based on sound reasons so that it is reasonable.

definition: A low stretch of land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it.

A small village sits at the bottom of a valley surrounded by tall hills.

form_sentences.sentence: Tea gardens spread across the green valleys of Sylhet during the rainy season.

definition: Worth a lot of money, or very useful and important to someone.
extra_senses: having worth or merit or value
something of value

form_sentences.sentence: Good health is more valuable than any amount of money in the bank.

The value of the old house has risen sharply in the past few years.

definition: The amount of money, or the importance, that something is considered to have.
extra_senses: the quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable
the amount (of money or goods or services) that is considered to be a fair equivalent for something else

A dictionary with clear examples adds real value to your English studies.

form_sentences.sentence: The bank's valuation of the flat was lower than the owner expected.

definition: A road vehicle, larger than a car, used to carry goods or passengers.

form_sentences.sentence: Delivery vans blocked the narrow road outside the market for almost an hour.

definition: The leaders of a movement or trend; the people at the front of new ideas.
extra_senses: any creative group active in the innovation and application of new concepts and techniques in a given field (especially in the arts)
the position of greatest importance or advancement; the leading position in any movement or field
examples: A group of young engineers is in the vanguard of the local software industry.

Women doctors were in the vanguard of the effort to teach villagers about clean water.
The band was in the vanguard of a new style that everyone soon copied.
Solar panels are in the vanguard of efforts to end load-shedding in remote areas.

form_sentences.sentence: Young coders in Dhaka are the vanguards of the city's new fintech startups.

definition: To defeat someone or something completely.
examples: The home team vanquished its rivals in the final and won the trophy.
In the legend, the hero vanquished a dragon with a single arrow.
She vanquished her fear of public speaking by practising in front of a mirror every day.
Doctors hope to vanquish the disease with a new vaccine.

form_sentences.sentence: The home team has vanquished its strongest rivals and reached the final.
The young hero is vanquishing the dragon in the children's storybook.

The vanquisher of the old champion celebrated with his team on the pitch.

definition: Lacking interest, energy or flavor; dull and boring.
extra_senses: lacking significance or liveliness or spirit or zest
examples: The vapid conversation about the weather lasted an hour.

Without spices, the soup tasted vapid and watery.

definition: A slight difference or change from what is usual or expected.

definition: Made up of many different kinds or forms, and not all the same.

definition: Marked with patches or spots of different colors.

definition: A range of different things of the same general kind.

form_sentences.sentence: The market sells many varieties of mango during the summer season.

definition: Of many different kinds or types, and not all the same.

distinctly dissimilar or unlike

definition: To be different from one another, or to change, depending on the situation.

form_sentences.sentence: The prices varied widely between the two markets last Friday.

definition: Extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

The company spent a vast sum on new machines, hoping to increase its output.

form_sentences.sentence: The lake seems vast when you stand at its edge during monsoon.

definition: A plant, or a part of a plant such as a root, leaf or stem, eaten as food.

examples: My mother buys fresh vegetables from the local market every Friday morning.

The actor still has a youthful energy that impresses audiences.

definition: Great energy and enthusiasm for a cause, an activity or a belief.
extra_senses: excessive fervor to do something or accomplish some end
prompt willingness
examples: The volunteers worked with great zeal to rebuild the school after the cyclone.
Her zeal for learning English led her to read one new article every day.
The new coach brought such zeal to training that even tired players smiled.
He started the business with youthful zeal, working late every night.
The club's zeal for planting trees changed the whole look of the neighborhood.

form_sentences.sentence: Zealous volunteers cleaned the riverbank before the school sports day.

definition: A person who is extremely enthusiastic about a cause or belief and may refuse to consider other views.
extra_senses: a fervent and even militant proponent of something
examples: My cousin is a fitness zealot who will not miss a workout even when he has a fever.
The cleanliness zealot in our office wipes every desk twice a day.
Football zealots argued until midnight about which team deserved the trophy.
As a zealot for recycling, she sorts every piece of rubbish, even at parties.
The zealot in our hostel insists that everyone must wake up at five for exercise.

definition: Very enthusiastic and eager, showing great energy in supporting a cause or doing something.
examples: The zealous volunteers worked all weekend to clean the riverbank.
She is a zealous student who stays after class to ask more questions.
A zealous fan, he has not missed a single home match in ten years.
The zealous young doctor visited every patient twice a day.
Zealous about recycling, he sorts every bit of rubbish at home.

form_sentences.sentence: The new coach seems zealous about improving our fitness before the tournament.
The younger members became more zealous about recycling after the workshop.
He approached his studies with zeal, rarely missing a single lecture.
The librarian zealously guarded the rare books in the reading room.

definition: The general mood, ideas and beliefs that are typical of a particular period in history.
examples: The song perfectly captured the zeitgeist of the late nineties, when everyone was talking about the internet.
Fashion designers try to read the zeitgeist so they know what people will want to wear next year.
Her novel reflects the zeitgeist of a generation worried about jobs and climate.
Short videos have become part of the zeitgeist, shaping how young people share news and jokes.
To understand the zeitgeist of an era, historians study its newspapers, songs and advertisements.

definition: The highest point of something, or the time when it is at its most successful or powerful.
examples: The sun reaches its zenith around noon, when shadows are shortest.
The singer's career was at its zenith when she filled the city's biggest stadium.
For many students, the zenith of the school year is the annual sports day.
The empire reached its zenith in the sixteenth century, with trade across three continents.
He retired at the zenith of his cricket career, while fans still wanted more.

form_sentences.sentence: Her career had several zeniths, each one higher than the last.

definition: Full of enthusiasm, energy and enjoyment.
examples: The zestful dancers filled the stage with energy and bright smiles.
She greeted the new term with a zestful attitude and a long list of plans.
My grandfather tells stories in a zestful way that keeps the children listening.
The coach's zestful speech lifted the team's spirits before the final.
A zestful game of football in the rain made everyone forget about the exams.

form_sentences.sentence: After a short nap, Karim felt zestful and ready for his evening class.
The second half of the wedding party was more zestful than the first.
He approached the new job with zest and a cheerful smile every morning.

definition: An area of land or a district that has a particular feature, purpose or set of rules.
extra_senses: regulate housing in; of certain areas of towns
any of the regions of the surface of the Earth loosely divided according to latitude or longitude
examples: The school declared the area around the main gate a no-parking zone during morning hours.
The old town is a busy commercial zone, full of wholesale shops and street vendors.
Our flight crossed into a different time zone, so we had to adjust our watches.
The factory zone near the highway has many small workshops that employ thousands of people.
The forest zone near the river is home to many birds, and visitors must stay on the trail.
